subject.title: [Feature]: SSRF 内网访问确认机制

question: Should OpenClaw add a browser private-network SSRF confirmation or allow/block policy, and which core policy shape is approved for browser navigation?
rationale: The request changes the browser egress security boundary and public config surface; source inspection shows no existing confirm or temporary-grant contract that automation can safely extend without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design A Staged Core Policy
options.body: Approve a narrow first phase such as explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata/link-local blocking before adding interactive confirmation.

options.title: Approve Interactive Confirmation Now
options.body: Commit to user-approval UX with timeout, rate-limit, audit, redirect, and channel/UI semantics across browser navigation paths before implementation.

options.title: Reject Core Expansion
options.body: Keep the current strict default plus hostname exceptions and document broad private-network access as an explicit trusted-environment opt-in only.

recommendation.title: Design A Staged Core Policy
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow first phase such as explicit allow/block policy plus non-overridable metadata/link-local blocking before adding interactive confirmation.

likelyOwner.reason: The sampled history and related security-boundary discussion make this the strongest routing candidate for the product/security decision.
